tfn.s: The article in Communications Psychology appeared in 2024.
tfn.why: The text says: "However, two psychologists writing in the journal Communications Psychology in 2024 discussed evidence that boredom may actually be increasing."

tfn.s: Different people experience boredom in different ways.
tfn.why: The text says: "People do not all feel boredom in the same way."

tfn.s: Children are more easily bored than adults, according to the study.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say whether children are more easily bored than adults.

tfn.s: The researchers proved that phones cause boredom.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "The researchers were discussing a possible explanation for a bigger change, not proving that every minute online creates boredom."

items.s: Their article presents an ____ of existing research.

tfn.s: Katy Tam and Michael Inzlicht wrote the 2024 perspective article.
tfn.why: The text says: "In a 2024 perspective article for Communications Psychology, researchers Katy Tam and Michael Inzlicht discussed evidence of rising boredom and proposed a possible explanation: digital media may sometimes make boredom worse instead of relieving it."

tfn.s: The article proves smartphones cause a worldwide rise in boredom.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "Their article presents an interpretation of existing research, not a single experiment proving that smartphones cause a worldwide increase."

tfn.s: The writers distinguish occasional boredom from persistent boredom.
tfn.why: The text says: "Researchers distinguish between an occasional boring moment and persistent boredom that interferes with wellbeing."

tfn.s: Boredom has risen fastest among teenagers.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say which age group has become most bored.

items.s: Someone can be busy yet deeply bored if their activities feel ____.

tfn.s: The researchers recommend a daily limit on phone use.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say that the researchers recommend any daily limit on phone use.

tfn.s: The writers suggest digital media may contribute to the feeling it promises to remove.
tfn.why: The text says: "In a 2024 perspective published in Communications Psychology, Katy Tam and Michael Inzlicht examined this paradox and proposed that digital media might contribute to the very feeling it promises to eliminate."

tfn.s: Someone can be busy and still feel deeply bored.
tfn.why: The text says: "Someone can be busy yet deeply bored if their activities feel meaningless."

tfn.s: All screen time has the same effect on boredom.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "Treating all screen time as interchangeable obscures those differences and risks replacing one simplistic explanation with another."
